prompt:
Write the appraiser's remarks (about 80 words) on a body shop repair estimate after a low-speed head-on collision. Describe the damage seen on the vehicle and the repair plan. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1362; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The bills show no repeated charges.
- The repair labor hours fit the damage.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
text: The front bumper cover is cracked across the center and the upper radiator support has a bend consistent with a frontal impact of this type, and the damage pattern lines up with the collision as described. The repair plan calls for replacing the bumper cover, straightening the support, and refinishing the adjacent panels. Labor hours are in line with the work required for this damage. The invoices reviewed show no repeated charges. A few light scratches on the rear quarter panel appear older than this loss and are noted separately, but they are not part of the proposed repair.
